title: Don't Test Where You Trained: Geographic Overlap Inflates End-to-End Driving Scores
abstract: arXiv:2611.28177v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In NAVSIMv1, the standard benchmark for end-to-end driving, $89.6\%$ of the test scenes lie within 4m of a training scene. We show that this geographic overlap inflates the reported scores. We propose a geographically disjoint split of NAVSIMv1 and an evaluation that compares models trained on either split on the same scenes, which neither has seen in training. All sensor-based models we test, DiffusionDrive, Latent TransFuser, and DrivoR, lose 3.4 to 6.1 PDMS points on these scenes, mainly by leaving the road and coming close to other objects, against 1.5 points for a baseline without sensors. The loss concentrates where a training drive of the original split passed the same place. At all other places, models trained on the original split are no better than those trained on the geographic split. Models trained on the original split predict road geometry that no camera can see. translated_title: 不要在你训练过的地方测试：地理重叠夸大了端到端驾驶分数
translated_abstract: 在端到端驾驶的标准基准NAVSIMv1中，89.6%的测试场景位于训练场景4米范围内。我们证明了这种地理重叠夸大了所报告的分数。我们提出了NAVSIMv1的一个地理上不相交的划分，并采用一种评估方法，在相同的、任一划分训练中都未见过的场景上比较分别在两个划分上训练的模型。我们测试的所有基于传感器的模型——DiffusionDrive、Latent TransFuser和DrivoR——在这些场景上损失了3.4到6.1个PDMS分，主要表现为驶离道路和靠近其他物体；相比之下，不使用传感器的基线仅损失1.5分。这种损失集中在原划分的训练驾驶数据曾经过相同地点的位置。在所有其他地方，在原划分上训练的模型并不比在地理划分上训练的模型更好。在原划分上训练的模型会预测出任何相机都无法看到的道路几何形状。即使移除辅助地图损失，这种差距依然存在，……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 论文揭示NAVSIMv1端到端驾驶基准中89.6%的测试场景与训练场景存在地理重叠从而夸大了分数，并提出地理不相交的划分进行评估，发现基于传感器的模型在未见过的地点上PDMS分数下降3.4至6.1分，且这种损失源于模型记忆了训练路线而非真正的驾驶能力。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that 89.6% of NAVSIMv1's test scenes geographically overlap with training scenes, inflating end-to-end driving benchmark scores, and proposes a geographically disjoint split showing sensor-based models lose 3.4 to 6.1 PDMS points on truly unseen locations, indicating memorization of training routes rather than genuine driving capability.
